title: Add compliance-probe toolchain: audit consistency checker + KMS region telemetry
author: Lina Chen
description: Motivation: customers and internal auditors need deterministic ways to validate that RBAC v2 decisions, KMS region scoping, and audit events remain consistent across installer upgrades and multi-region mirrors. This PR introduces a first-class compliance probe toolchain packaged with the private installer that performs sampled audit consistency checks, surfaces KMS region telemetry, and provides an operator consent reporter for post-deploy review. Summary of changes: 1) new runtime subcommand 'redwood-installer probe compliance' which can be run in dry-run or enforce mode; 2) audit-consistency-checker: samples audit streams (Kafka/S3 hooks) and validates event ordering, immutable fields, and KMS region headers against the policy decision logs; 3) kms-region-telemetry: collects per-request KMS region hints, region pin violations, and latency histograms, emitting a compact telemetry envelope to the observability service; 4) consent-reporter: aggregates operator approvals and timed attestation envelopes signed with tenant-scoped CMKs for traceability; 5) RBACv2 linter integration: new lint rule set to catch attribute scoping and region-anchored role templates during installer render; 6) docs and runbook: step-by-step compliance-runbook and upgrade notes. Backwards compatibility: feature is opt-in and disabled by default; probes run locally or as a separate job in the installer control-plane; nothing mutating by default. Migration and rollout: operator can enable via values.yaml flag 'complianceProbe.enabled: true' or CLI '--enable-compliance-probe'; recommend dry-run for 72 hours before switching to enforced checks; the consent-reporter requires KMS CMK permissions (see docs) and will no-op if unconfigured. Security considerations: probe signs telemetry envelopes with a installer-attest key; KMS usage is limited to region metadata and attestation signing; we added strict scope checks to avoid key exposure. Testing: unit tests for checker rules, integration tests against a mini-Kafka audit fixture, e2e run for installer with a two-region mirror. Observability: new metrics 'compliance.probe.sample_rate', 'compliance.kms.region_mismatch', 'compliance.audit.stability_score'. Implementation notes and rationale: the checker uses a timed-window replayer strategy to avoid stateful long-lived compares across tenants; instead it computes stable hashes for event prefixes and compares proof windows across mirrors. This minimizes retention while providing high-confidence divergence detection. Related work: references ENG-5012 design doc, earlier residency telemetry prototypes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Docs & runbook - [x] CI passing - [x] Security review comments addressed Release impact: opt-in; no immediate behavior changes for existing installs.

release_notes: Add an opt-in 'compliance probe' packaged with the private installer: provides sampled audit consistency checks, KMS region telemetry, and an operator consent reporter. Default off; see docs/compliance-runbook.md for enablement and rollout guidance.
notes: This PR targets operational compliance controls rather than policy changes; it's intentionally configured as opt-in to avoid unexpected behavior during upgrades. The runbook includes a recommended 72-hour dry-run and checklist for KMS entitlement. Follow-up work planned to wire probe telemetry into the Console compliance dashboard.
impact_statement: Low-risk opt-in feature; adds observability and non-mutating checks by default; requires KMS permission to enable consent-report signing.
test_plan: Unit test coverage for linter and checker rules; integration test using kafka-mini fixture; e2e installer smoke with two-region mirror; manual dry-run in staging for 72h prior to production enforcement.
